messages:
Nikhil Sharma: we should align today on launch gates for quickstart templates. what counts as “ready” for ship (repo + docs)? trying to avoid a soft-launch that becomes permanent :grimacing:

Talia Benson: +1. I’m getting asked for a go/no-go checklist. Can we define hard requirements vs “nice to have” and who signs off?

Alex Martinez: yes please. DX can commit to a date, but only if gates are crisp. also want to prevent: docs drift, missing retries/timeouts, and “works on my laptop” only.

Marissa Cole: from Console side: minimum is that templates emit the telemetry contract so the default dashboards actually light up. If people run it and Console is empty, that’s a failed onboarding.

Paula Mendes: +1. I’d propose a “contract compliance” gate:
- required trace attrs present (request_id, tenant_id, route, model)
- metrics emitted (latency, tokens in/out, error_class)
- log correlation fields present
- cardinality limits respected (no user_email etc)

Henry Cho: API ergonomics piece: do we require request_id echo + traceparent passthrough in hosted before launch? templates assume they can join traces.

Marissa Cole: not strictly. templates can generate request_id client-side + propagate, but we should be consistent. If hosted echoes `x-request-id` and forwards `traceparent` it’s way nicer.

Nikhil Sharma: hosted can take the request_id echo change (already on my list). but I don’t want to block launch on it unless it’s mandatory.

Elliot Price: docs gate from my side:
- landing page + per-template walkthrough published
- code snippets are extracted from repo (no hand-written examples)
- “production checklist” page exists and is linked from each template doc
- clear “Hosted now / Dedicated later / Private considerations” callouts

Wei Chen: + requirement that Quickstart docs match the env var contract exactly. we’ve been burned before.

Monica Patel: SDK gate: templates must use the standardized retry/timeout helpers (or equivalent) so we don’t create new ticket drivers:
- explicit timeouts (connect + request)
- 429 retry/backoff w/ jitter + respect Retry-After
- streaming reconnect guidance (where applicable) + idempotency key usage

Sean Gallagher: SRE gate: CI smoke tests should run the happy path against staging and verify telemetry emitted. also need sane default alert thresholds (burn-rate style) so we don’t ship “pager by default”.

Naomi Feldman: security gate: no secrets in repo, `.env.example` only, recommend secret manager for deploy, plus:
- dependency pinning
- tool calling allow-list defaults
- PII guidance + logging hygiene (no raw prompts/docs in INFO logs)

Nikhil Sharma: ok let’s structure this.
Gates I’m hearing:
A) Template functionality
B) Observability + telemetry compliance
C) Safety + security defaults
D) Docs readiness
E) CI + release
F) Support readiness (??)

Dylan Brooks: please include support readiness. otherwise Product gets pinged when 429/streaming questions show up.

Talia Benson: can we list *minimum* gates for v1 launch? then we can backlog “nice to have”.

Alex Martinez: minimum should still be production-shaped, not “tutorial-grade”.

Marissa Cole: minimum for Console/telemetry:
1) traces show end-to-end spans with request_id/tenant_id
2) token usage metrics emitted + tags: model, route, status
3) error taxonomy: timeouts vs 429 vs 5xx vs validation
4) dashboard import instructions work

Paula Mendes: also: budget/cost attribution needs at least route + model; tenant_id optional for single-tenant quickstart but should be present as a placeholder.

Wei Chen: + docs need a “what telemetry you should see” section. a screenshot + how to click through in Console.

Monica Patel: for SDK, I’d call it “must”:
- timeouts enabled by default
- retries only for safe errors (429/503/ETIMEDOUT etc), no retry on 4xx validation
- max retry time bounded (don’t hang forever)

Sean Gallagher: and graceful shutdown (SIGTERM) so people don’t corrupt local vector DB / in-flight requests.

Naomi Feldman: plus “safe prompt/tooling defaults”: tool allow-list + tool timeout wrapper + output schema validation. even if simplified.

Henry Cho: question: are we gating on all templates or can we launch RAG first? (catalog says RAG + agents + combined)

Alex Martinez: I’d prefer we don’t half-launch. marketing + docs IA is “choose your template”. if agents is missing, it looks broken.

Elliot Price: agree. docs nav gets messy if we ship 1 of 3.

Nikhil Sharma: ok so gate = all three templates present (py + ts). any language gaps acceptable? (Go is “selective”)

Talia Benson: propose:
- v1 requires Python + TypeScript for all three
- Go optional (advisor only)

Connor O'Brien: release gate: we should tag a version (v1.0.0) and have a compat matrix with SDK versions. Otherwise docs can’t pin.

Wei Chen: + deprecation policy link (even if short). people will copy/paste.

Dylan Brooks: support gate suggestions:
- known issues doc populated (429 behavior, proxy streaming disconnects, CORS)
- “how to file a ticket” includes request_id and how to export traces
- canned responses/macros (at least internal) for top 5 issues

Sean Gallagher: also add rate limit guidance: “don’t retry instantly, use exponential backoff, honor Retry-After”. that alone cuts noise.

Nikhil Sharma: ok, let’s turn this into explicit go/no-go criteria.
Draft MINIMUM launch gates:
1) Templates: RAG, Agents, RAG+Agents shipped in redwood-quickstarts with local run + container run (docker compose)
2) CI: smoke test for each template against staging passes on main; includes a check that telemetry emitted (at least one trace + metrics)
3) Telemetry contract v1 compliance (required attrs/metrics/log fields)
4) SDK safe defaults: timeouts + retry/backoff patterns used in templates; streaming guidance included
5) Security: secrets policy followed; tool allow-list + tool timeouts + output schema validation; PII/logging guidance
6) Docs: landing page + walkthroughs + production checklist; snippets sourced from repo; env var contract matches
7) Observability pack: default dashboards importable + README
8) Support: known issues page + “include request_id” troubleshooting section
Signoffs:
- DX (Alex)
- Product (Nikhil)
- Console/Telemetry (Marissa/Paula)
- Security (Naomi)
- SRE (Sean)
- Docs (Elliot)

Thoughts? what’s controversial / missing?

Marissa Cole: looks right. I’d change (3) to specify exact attributes so we don’t debate later. Paula can drop the list.

Paula Mendes: I’ll paste the required set here later today + add a simple validator script requirement (fail fast if missing env vars/attrs).

Naomi Feldman: good w/ security gate but make sure it doesn’t imply “fully compliant” for regulated workloads. wording should be “secure defaults + guidance” not “HIPAA-ready”.

Elliot Price: +1. also docs gate should include “Dedicated/Private considerations” section but can be brief (networking, auth, audit logs). not full guide.

Sean Gallagher: CI gate: allow one rerun for flake? (staging can be noisy). but we should track flake rate.

Connor O'Brien: release gate: tags + changelog + ownership for patch releases (DX on-call rotation). Not required pre-launch but required within 1 week?

Alex Martinez: I’d rather we require release automation before launch. otherwise we ship v1 then scramble.

Nikhil Sharma: ok, move release automation into minimum gate as #9:
9) Version tag + changelog + compatibility matrix (SDK versions) + ownership rotation documented

Henry Cho: any gate on API side changes? request_id echo?

Marissa Cole: not a hard gate. but let’s add as “should” in the checklist and track as follow-up.

Talia Benson: I’ll write this up as “Launch gates v1” and schedule a 30-min go/no-go the week before. Can each signer confirm they’re good owning their checks?

Monica Patel: SDK team can own #4; we’ll publish the helper usage in both languages.

Dylan Brooks: support will own #8 w/ Dev Patel + Owen. we’ll need links from docs.

Alex Martinez: DX owns #1/#2/#6/#9 coordination. Thanks all. once Talia posts the doc, we’ll pin it in #devex + #product.

Nikhil Sharma: :thumbsup: decision then: launch = when all minimum gates pass. no “soft ship” without docs + telemetry. Talia, please include “no-go examples” (e.g., templates run but no metrics, or docs snippet drift).

Talia Benson: will do. I’ll also add an explicit “known issues allowed” section (must be documented, no Sev-1).

Sean Gallagher: add: no default pager alerts. dashboards ok; alerts opt-in w/ sane thresholds.

Marissa Cole: +1. alerts shipped but disabled by default. doc says “enable after you tune”.

Wei Chen: I’ll add a docs note: “alerts are templates, not promises” + how to adjust.

Naomi Feldman: and include security note: “don’t log raw docs/prompts” in bold.

Nikhil Sharma: perfect. closing the loop here once doc link is ready.
